Results
Fabrication and characterizations of nano-metal diborides

We achieve the structural transformation of metal disulphide into metal diboride $\left(\mathrm{M S}_{2}+\mathrm{B}\rightarrow\mathrm{M B}_{2}+\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{x}}\right)$ undera $\mathsf{K C I-C s C I}$ molten salt condition (Fig. la and Supplementary Table 1). The gaseous sulfurcontaining products may consist of $\mathsf{S}_{2},\mathsf{S}_{4},\mathsf{S}_{8},\mathsf{a n d}\:\mathsf{B}_{2}\mathsf{S}_{3}$ at the reaction temperatures $(1000-1100^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ , while $S_{2}$ is considered to be the most abundant species31. We calculate the reaction enthalpy and entropic term to determine the Gibbs free enthalpy of the chemical reaction $\left(\Delta G=\Delta H-\mathrm{T}\Delta S\right)$ .As exhibited in Fig. lb and Supplementary Table 2, the entropic term TΔs of the gaseous sulfur-containing products is the dominant part of the total Gibbs energy. After reaching a certain temperature, the entropy gain would drive the reaction from a thermodynamically unfeasible process to a thermodynamically spontaneous process. According to the entropy-driven route, we can synthesize nine monometallic diborides, including MB2$(\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{T i},\mathsf{Z r},\mathsf{H f})$ V, Nb, Ta, Mo, W, and Re). The powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) paterns F in Fig. lc confirm that the majority of as-synthesized samples are pure transition metal diboride phases. The morphologies of these borides are revealed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Supplementary Fig. 2).$\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ and $\mathsf{M o B}_{2}$ _possess a typical nanosheet structure,$\mathsf{W B}_{2}$

shows a nanowire morphology, and other $\mathsf{M B}_{2}$ samples $(\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{Ti},\mathsf{Zr},\mathsf{Hf}$ V, Nb, and Re) are composed of nanoparticles with sizes ranging fom 50 to 200nm. Most of these $\mathsf{M B}_{2}$ samples possess large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface areas within the range of $40-60\ m^{2}\ g^{-1}$ (Fig. ld and Supplementary Table 3), which are obviously higher than those of borides obtained by conventional hightemperature ceramic method

We have compared the acid corrosion resistance and BET surface area of nine metal diborides synthesized above. Compared with $\mathsf{TaB}_{2}$ the $\mathsf{T i B}_{2},\mathsf{Z r B}_{2},\mathsf{H f B}_{2},\mathsf{V B}_{2},\mathsf{C r B}_{2},\mathsf{M o B}_{2},$ ,and $\mathsf{W B}_{2}$ show more severe metal dissolution in acid (Supplementary Table $^{3)}$ .After the exposure to $0.5\mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S O}_{4}$ over a wek (Supplementary Fig. 3), almost no Ta species are leached in the acidic solution, and $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ retains its pristine crystal structure well. Discussion

In conclusion, we have demonstrated an entropy-driven disulphide-todiboride transition route strategy that can be operated to synthesize large-surface-area metal diborides as the promising support of $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ nanocatalysts. As a demonstration, we have prepared $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ _-supported $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ nanocatalyst $\mathrm{(i.e.,~IrO_{2}@TaB_{2})}$ ,which displays uniformly distributed $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ nanoparticles $(\sim1.5\mathrm{n m})$ ,highly conductive networks, and great acidic corrosion resistance. Impressively, the as-prepared $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 2 catalysts with an optimized $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ content exhibit a 10times higher iridium mass activity than $\mathrm{IrO_{2}},$ ,while showing lower iridium leaching during acidic OER. When integrated into a PEMWE, the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 2anode cell requires 2.0Vto attain 3.06 Acm-(reaching the US DOE 2023  target), under a much lower PGM loadings of $0.15\mathrm{m g}_{\mathrm{i r}}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ and $0.27mg_{Pt}cm^{-2}$ than DOE 2023 target (PGM loading of $\mathbf{1}\mathrm{m g}\mathrm{c m}^{-2})$ ). Our findings highlight the rational design of highly conductive, corrosion resistance, and large surface area materials as $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ _ supports for acidic OER, and stimulate practical applications of low-iridium-loading anode catalyst layers in industrial PEMwE.

Materials synthesis

The metal diborides were synthesized by borothermal reduction in a molten salt medium (KCl-CsCl) with an equal molar ratio. The metal disulfide, boron powder, and molten salt are ground thoroughly in a mortar for 0.5h. Then the mixture was transferred into a corundum boat and heated at 900-1100 C under Ar atmosphere in a tubular furnace, and the heating rate was $10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}/$ .'min (Supplementary Table 1).After thorough cooling, the mixture was repeatedly washed with water and ethanol to remove soluble molten salts and byproducts. The final prepared metal diborides were dried at 80 C for 12 h.

The suspension was ultrasonically dispersed for 30 min and then dried at 90 C for 5h. Then the mixed powder was ground and heated in a muffle furnace at $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}_{i}$ /min to 350 ℃ for 1h.After naturally cooling down, the product was washed fully with ethanol and water to remove residual salts, and the black catalyst powder was dried in an oven at 90 ℃C for 12 h to get $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 2.
